title: Better in every group, worse overall
hook: Treatment A beats B for small kidney stones. It beats B for large ones. Overall, A loses. How?

scenes.say: Treatment A beats B for small kidney stones. It beats B for large ones. Overall, A loses. How?
scenes.show: Better in every group. Worse overall.

scenes.say: It's Simpson's paradox, with real data from a 1986 kidney stone study.
scenes.note: Source: Charig et al. (1986), BMJ · rates computed from the original counts

scenes.say: Small stones: A {g0_a}, B {g0_b}. Large stones: A {g1_a}, B {g1_b}.
A was used far more on the hard large-stone cases. Mixing groups flipped the conclusion.
Before trusting a total, ask whether the groups inside it are actually alike.

takeaway: Before trusting a total, ask whether the groups inside it are actually alike.
